# Pavan Nallamothu - Offensive Security Research (full)

> Offensive security researcher. 12 published CVEs across Apple, CISA, NSA, AutoGPT, yt-dlp and BlueprintUE, plus two open-access papers (Zenodo). This file expands the manifest in /llms.txt with the full technical body of each item. Every item carries the independent third-party advisory that credits "pavanchow" / "Pavan Nallamothu". The researcher/credentials hub is https://pavanchow.gitlab.io/.

## CVEs

### CVE-2026-43763 - Apple macOS ATS sandbox file-read (medium)
A permissions issue in Apple Type Services (ATS) allowed a sandboxed process file-read access outside its container. Fixed across macOS Tahoe, Sequoia, and Sonoma. Co-credited by Apple to Pavan Nallamothu and Jared Reyes.
Independent source: https://support.apple.com/en-us/128067

### CVE-2026-33234 - AutoGPT SSRF via user-controlled SMTP server (medium, CVSS 5.0)
SendEmailBlock passes a user-supplied smtp_server / smtp_port straight to smtplib.SMTP() with no IP validation, bypassing the platform's validate_url_host() and BLOCKED_IP_NETWORKS blocklist. Affects versions 0.1.0 through 0.6.51. This is the case study for the EPI-SSRF (Egress-Path-Incomplete SSRF) model.
Independent source: https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT/security/advisories/GHSA-4jwj-6mg5-wrwf

### CVE-2026-50023 - yt-dlp dangerous file creation (high, CVSS 8.3)
The CVE-2024-38519 allowlist still permitted .desktop, .url, and .webloc for --write-link, letting a remote attacker write malicious OS-shortcut files during media/subtitle downloads and bypass the prior fix. Fixed in 2026.06.09.
Independent source: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c6mh-fpjc-4pr3

### CVE-2026-63133 - CISA Malcolm uncontrolled resource consumption / inode-exhaustion DoS (medium)
safe-extract.py places no cap on archive entry count, depth, or uncompressed size. A small malicious archive exhausts inodes, crashing the filebeat processing pipeline and blinding the SOC's network-visibility tool.
Independent source: https://github.com/cisagov/Malcolm/security/advisories/GHSA-c35g-mgc3-95rx

### CVE-2026-63134 - CISA Malcolm path traversal in archive extraction (medium)
safe-extract.py protects file entries with libarchive secure flags but creates directory entries with raw os.makedirs(), with no traversal protection, allowing arbitrary directory creation outside the extraction root.
Independent source: https://github.com/cisagov/Malcolm/security/advisories/GHSA-65mm-vgrw-vqx4

### CVE-2026-63177 - CISA Malcolm authorization bypass via URI-normalization differential / RBAC (high)
A URI-normalization differential between the reverse proxy and the application backend lets an authenticated user bypass ROLE_UPLOAD checks and reach the upload/processing endpoint without the required role.
Independent source: https://github.com/cisagov/Malcolm/security/advisories/GHSA-m5fr-rv3h-xg2r

### CVE-2026-63013 - NSA skills-service privilege escalation (high, CVSS 8.8)
Three admin-group assignment endpoints grant admin roles with no caller-authorization check. Any authenticated user takes over any project, quiz, or global badge, reading and destructively deleting data. CVE assigned, MITRE record pending; the GitHub Security Advisory is the canonical source.
Independent source: https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/skills-service/security/advisories/GHSA-67x3-r85f-822r

### CVE-2026-63014 - NSA skills-service cross-project IDOR (moderate, CVSS 4.3)
A non-greedy regex in the authorization filter matches only the first projects/{id} segment, letting any project admin enumerate subject IDs and read subject/skill names across tenant boundaries. CVE assigned, MITRE record pending; the GitHub Security Advisory is the canonical source.
Independent source: https://github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/skills-service/security/advisories/GHSA-p527-vjfp-c43p

### CVE-2026-40585 - blueprintUE non-expiring password-reset tokens (medium)
findUserIDFromEmailAndToken() queries only email + token and never checks the password_reset_at timestamp, so a 128-char CSPRNG reset token stays valid forever until consumed or overwritten. Fixed in 4.2.0.
Independent source: https://github.com/blueprintue/blueprintue-self-hosted-edition/security/advisories/GHSA-qr65-6vp8-whjf

### CVE-2026-40586 - blueprintUE missing brute-force protection on login (high)
The login handler performs no throttling of any kind: no IP-based rate limiting, lockout, or per-account counter. Enables unlimited brute force, dictionary attacks, and credential stuffing. Fixed in 4.2.0.
Independent source: https://github.com/blueprintue/blueprintue-self-hosted-edition/security/advisories/GHSA-m6c2-6p3h-8jv2

### CVE-2026-40587 - blueprintUE insufficient session expiration after credential change (medium)
Password change and reset flows update only the password column and never destroy active sessions, so a compromised session retains full access even after the victim changes their password. Fixed in 4.2.0.
Independent source: https://github.com/blueprintue/blueprintue-self-hosted-edition/security/advisories/GHSA-gqpq-x62g-p4mg

### CVE-2026-40588 - blueprintUE account takeover via password change without current-password check (high)
The password-change flow does not verify the current password before accepting a new one, so an attacker with a momentary session (XSS, sidejacking, physical access) can change the victim's password and take over the account permanently. Fixed in 4.2.0.
Independent source: https://github.com/blueprintue/blueprintue-self-hosted-edition/security/advisories/GHSA-73f2-p9jr-m44x

## Advisories without a CVE

### GHSA-w8gq-4v5x-xrrm - CISA Malcolm unauthenticated script execution via CSRF (high, CVSS 7.1)
Unauthenticated script execution via CSRF in the kiosk /script_call endpoint. Published 2026-08-24.
Independent source: https://github.com/cisagov/Malcolm/security/advisories/GHSA-w8gq-4v5x-xrrm

### GHSA-86h3-7rf8-8j34 - CISA Malcolm missing server-to-server auth (moderate, CVSS 4.2)
Missing server-to-server (s2s) authentication on the Hedgehog Sensor Arkime reachback port. Published 2026-08-24.
Independent source: https://github.com/cisagov/Malcolm/security/advisories/GHSA-86h3-7rf8-8j34

## Papers

### SSRF Beyond HTTP: Egress-Path-Incomplete Guards in AI Agent Platforms
A formal egress-path-incomplete (EPI) SSRF model instantiated on CVE-2026-33234 in AutoGPT. Zenodo, 2026. Author: Nallamothu, Pavan.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22075470 - record: https://zenodo.org/records/22075470 - landing page: https://pavanchow.github.io/papers/ssrf-beyond-http.html

### Trusting the Filename: File-Write Attacks from Untrusted Archive and Download Metadata
File-write attacks driven by attacker-controlled archive and download metadata, across three 2026 CVEs. Zenodo, 2026. Author: Nallamothu, Pavan.
DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22075439 - record: https://zenodo.org/records/22075439 - landing page: https://pavanchow.github.io/papers/trusting-the-filename.html - second DOI: https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202608.2314.v1 (Preprints.org, Crossref-registered, MDPI AG)

## Defined terms
- EPI-SSRF (Egress-Path-Incomplete SSRF): server-side request forgery where an egress guard validates only part of the request surface, leaving an alternate egress path (e.g. a non-HTTP protocol such as SMTP) unchecked. Formalized in "SSRF Beyond HTTP", instantiated on CVE-2026-33234.

## Open-source builds (Rust, each its own repository and live page) - 61 from-scratch systems tools

### Compilers, languages, and runtimes
- Alchemist - https://github.com/pavanchow/alchemist - https://pavanchow.github.io/alchemist/ - a compiler that lexes, parses, and lowers a small language to stack bytecode, then runs it on a bundled VM
- Anvil - https://github.com/pavanchow/anvil - https://pavanchow.github.io/anvil/ - a compiler backend that lowers SSA to a target machine with graph-coloring register allocation
- Esperanto - https://github.com/pavanchow/esperanto - https://pavanchow.github.io/esperanto/ - a small statically-typed language with type inference
- Kindling - https://github.com/pavanchow/kindling - https://pavanchow.github.io/kindling/ - a dynamically typed language with a bytecode compiler and a stack-based virtual machine
- Mirage - https://github.com/pavanchow/mirage - https://pavanchow.github.io/mirage/ - a small bytecode virtual machine with its own instruction set, assembler, and runner
- Sprite - https://github.com/pavanchow/sprite - https://pavanchow.github.io/sprite/ - a tiny embeddable scripting language with lexer, recursive-descent parser, and tree-walking interpreter
- Whetstone - https://github.com/pavanchow/whetstone - https://pavanchow.github.io/whetstone/ - a compiler optimizer with constant folding, propagation, and algebraic simplification
- Phantom - https://github.com/pavanchow/phantom - https://pavanchow.github.io/phantom/ - a CHIP-8 emulator with a fully unit-tested CPU core

### Operating systems and kernels
- Aurora - https://github.com/pavanchow/aurora - https://pavanchow.github.io/aurora/ - an amnesic aarch64 kernel that runs in RAM, encrypts its vault in memory, and wipes secrets on exit
- Bedrock - https://github.com/pavanchow/bedrock - https://pavanchow.github.io/bedrock/ - a from-scratch virtual CPU, assembler, and preemptive OS kernel you can boot in the browser
- Chronos - https://github.com/pavanchow/chronos - https://pavanchow.github.io/chronos/ - a CPU scheduler running FIFO, SJF, round-robin, priority, and MLFQ over real processes
- Cocoon - https://github.com/pavanchow/cocoon - https://pavanchow.github.io/cocoon/ - a rootless Linux container runtime using namespaces, pivot_root, and dropped capabilities
- Conch - https://github.com/pavanchow/conch - https://pavanchow.github.io/conch/ - a Unix shell with a hand-written tokenizer, pipeline parser, and process wiring
- Emberchip - https://github.com/pavanchow/emberchip - https://pavanchow.github.io/emberchip/ - a deterministic RTOS simulator on an emulated microcontroller with priority inheritance
- Honeycomb - https://github.com/pavanchow/honeycomb - https://pavanchow.github.io/honeycomb/ - a readable global memory allocator with live stats
- Ignition - https://github.com/pavanchow/ignition - https://pavanchow.github.io/ignition/ - a deterministic boot sequence simulator with an MBR parser, zero dependencies
- Nesthost - https://github.com/pavanchow/nesthost - https://pavanchow.github.io/nesthost/ - a deterministic type-1 hypervisor simulator that runs several guest VMs
- Pane - https://github.com/pavanchow/pane - https://pavanchow.github.io/pane/ - a dependency-free tiling window manager engine
- Seedcore - https://github.com/pavanchow/seedcore - https://pavanchow.github.io/seedcore/ - a deterministic microkernel simulator with threads, address spaces, and synchronization
- Terrarium - https://github.com/pavanchow/terrarium - https://pavanchow.github.io/terrarium/ - a from-scratch scripting sandbox that runs untrusted code under resource limits

### Security and cryptography
- Cipherlock - https://github.com/pavanchow/cipherlock - https://pavanchow.github.io/cipherlock/ - encryption toolkit with from-scratch ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (RFC 8439 vectors)
- Gatekeeper - https://github.com/pavanchow/gatekeeper - https://pavanchow.github.io/gatekeeper/ - an auth server with HMAC-SHA256 signed tokens and salted password hashing, no crypto crates
- Ironchain - https://github.com/pavanchow/ironchain - https://pavanchow.github.io/ironchain/ - a from-scratch proof-of-work blockchain whose only primitive is SHA-256
- Lint-Owl - https://github.com/pavanchow/lint-owl - https://pavanchow.github.io/lint-owl/ - static analyzer returning the data-flow path from source to sink
- Oracle - https://github.com/pavanchow/oracle - https://pavanchow.github.io/oracle/ - query language whose result is an attack path across identity and network graphs
- Unweave - https://github.com/pavanchow/unweave - https://pavanchow.github.io/unweave/ - EVM bytecode disassembler that reconstructs intent and flags dangerous opcodes
- Veilproof - https://github.com/pavanchow/veilproof - https://pavanchow.github.io/veilproof/ - a zero-knowledge proof system with no crypto crates and no elliptic curves

### Networking and web
- Datagram - https://github.com/pavanchow/datagram - https://pavanchow.github.io/datagram/ - a TCP reliable-transport engine over a simulated lossy link
- Echofront - https://github.com/pavanchow/echofront - https://pavanchow.github.io/echofront/ - a layer 7 reverse proxy and load balancer with health checks and circuit breaking
- Ferryman - https://github.com/pavanchow/ferryman - https://pavanchow.github.io/ferryman/ - a load balancer with round-robin, weighted, least-connections, and seeded random strategies
- Hearth - https://github.com/pavanchow/hearth - https://pavanchow.github.io/hearth/ - an HTTP server from scratch on std::net, no framework
- Kaleidoscope - https://github.com/pavanchow/kaleidoscope - https://pavanchow.github.io/kaleidoscope/ - a browser engine with HTML parser, CSS parser, cascade, block layout, and paint
- Lighthouse - https://github.com/pavanchow/lighthouse - https://pavanchow.github.io/lighthouse/ - a browser rendering engine that runs HTML and CSS through parse, layout, and paint
- Rift - https://github.com/pavanchow/rift - https://pavanchow.github.io/rift/ - reverse proxy whose routing rules are a compiled DSL
- Riverbed - https://github.com/pavanchow/riverbed - https://pavanchow.github.io/riverbed/ - a message broker with topics, wildcard subscriptions, and bounded per-subscriber queues
- Semaphore - https://github.com/pavanchow/semaphore - https://pavanchow.github.io/semaphore/ - length-prefixed framing codec plus a typed request/response protocol over TCP
- Tollgate - https://github.com/pavanchow/tollgate - https://pavanchow.github.io/tollgate/ - a from-scratch API gateway where routing, auth, and rate limiting are a pure pipeline

### Data and storage
- Archipelago - https://github.com/pavanchow/archipelago - https://pavanchow.github.io/archipelago/ - a distributed file system with quorum writes, self-healing, and content-addressed chunks
- Conduit - https://github.com/pavanchow/conduit - https://pavanchow.github.io/conduit/ - a from-scratch PostgreSQL driver speaking the v3 wire protocol with hand-written SCRAM-SHA-256
- Flashvault - https://github.com/pavanchow/flashvault - https://pavanchow.github.io/flashvault/ - an LRU cache with TTL expiry, a capacity bound, and live stats
- Flint - https://github.com/pavanchow/flint - https://pavanchow.github.io/flint/ - embedded single-binary key-value store, append-only log with in-memory index
- Keystone - https://github.com/pavanchow/keystone - https://pavanchow.github.io/keystone/ - a durable, ordered, embedded key-value store written from scratch
- Ledgerstone - https://github.com/pavanchow/ledgerstone - https://pavanchow.github.io/ledgerstone/ - an embedded relational database with a real SQL subset and a hand-written executor
- Strata - https://github.com/pavanchow/strata - https://pavanchow.github.io/strata/ - a file system inside one container file: superblock, bitmap allocator, inodes, directories
- Timelace - https://github.com/pavanchow/timelace - https://pavanchow.github.io/timelace/ - content-addressed version-control core with blobs, trees, and commits
- Trailhead - https://github.com/pavanchow/trailhead - https://pavanchow.github.io/trailhead/ - full-text search engine with inverted index and TF-IDF ranking

### Graphics, audio, and machine learning
- Forge - https://github.com/pavanchow/forge - https://pavanchow.github.io/forge/ - a dependency-free 2D game engine with an ECS, a fixed-timestep loop, and impulse-based physics
- Loom - https://github.com/pavanchow/loom - https://pavanchow.github.io/loom/ - a dependency-free retained-mode GUI layout engine
- Newton - https://github.com/pavanchow/newton - https://pavanchow.github.io/newton/ - a 2D physics engine with semi-implicit Euler, circle collision, and impulse resolution
- Prism - https://github.com/pavanchow/prism - https://pavanchow.github.io/prism/ - a software rasterizer that draws 3D triangles on the CPU with a z-buffer, no GPU
- Reverb - https://github.com/pavanchow/reverb - https://pavanchow.github.io/reverb/ - audio synthesis engine with oscillators, an ADSR envelope, and a WAV writer
- Synapse - https://github.com/pavanchow/synapse - https://pavanchow.github.io/synapse/ - reverse-mode autograd engine that trains a network on XOR

### Developer tools
- Atelier - https://github.com/pavanchow/atelier - https://pavanchow.github.io/atelier/ - a dependency-free code-intelligence engine with go to definition, find references, diagnostics, and rename
- Bloodhound - https://github.com/pavanchow/bloodhound - https://pavanchow.github.io/bloodhound/ - a portable time-travel debugger that steps backward through a running program
- Metronome - https://github.com/pavanchow/metronome - https://pavanchow.github.io/metronome/ - cron scheduler around a pure, unit-tested schedule engine
- Quartermaster - https://github.com/pavanchow/quartermaster - https://pavanchow.github.io/quartermaster/ - a from-scratch package manager with a PubGrub dependency resolver that explains conflicts
- Quill - https://github.com/pavanchow/quill - https://pavanchow.github.io/quill/ - a dependency-free editable text buffer backed by a piece table
- Quorum - https://github.com/pavanchow/quorum - https://pavanchow.github.io/quorum/ - a deterministic Raft consensus simulator with leader election and log replication
- Relay - https://github.com/pavanchow/relay - https://pavanchow.github.io/relay/ - a from-scratch CI/CD engine whose scheduler is a pure, deterministic DAG executor
- Shepherd - https://github.com/pavanchow/shepherd - https://pavanchow.github.io/shepherd/ - a Kubernetes-style reconciliation control loop that schedules pods onto nodes
- Stopwatch - https://github.com/pavanchow/stopwatch - https://pavanchow.github.io/stopwatch/ - a profiler with a call tree of self time and total time
